title: White Tower catalog file
description: An agent's catalog file, catalog.json, format whitetower.catalog.v1: the MCP servers, tools and models enabled for the agent and those observed for it, and the deployment's redaction rules (docs/contracts/module-contract-v0.1.md, section 7.7). A closed document: step V7 refuses a file that does not match this schema (parse_error).

redaction.description: The deployment's redaction rules, which EP-14 applies beyond its own.

url_prefixes.description: Normalized http or https URLs that end with /, after each of which the next path segment is a secret. A normalized URL has a lowercase scheme and host, no user information, query or fragment, and a path that RFC 3986 allows.

flags.description: Names of flags whose values are secrets, matched exactly against a flag's name, which follows its leading dashes and ends before its first =: a name that starts with - or holds = would never match.

reference.description: The server's reference, as section 4.10 computes it.

items.description: A tool, which carries what makes up its reference (section 4.10): an MCP tool its server and its name, a built-in tool its provider, its type and its name, and any other tool its name alone.

type.description: A built-in tool's type, as its provider names it.

args.description: The tool's arguments that policies may see (section 6.11).

allOf.description: A built-in tool has no definition, and an approved tool of any other kind has its definition pinned: a tool without a definition hash can never be approved (section 4.10).

endpoint.description: The normalized base URL of the endpoint (section 4.10).

digest.description: The pinned digest of the model's weights.

serverKey.description: A server's key: a slug of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, of at most 63 characters (section 4.10).

argument.description: A declared argument: its name, which is its key in the tool's record of context.args, its path in the call's arguments, through objects only, its transform, and its type as Cedar names it. A property whose name holds . or : cannot be declared, and a transform applies to strings only.
